title: Purposes of Life: 9 Commands / Commands 5th to 7th

questions.question: What is the fifth aim about doing with the special gifts Allah placed in a person?
questions.answer: Using them carefully and showing them with awareness before Allah.

questions.question: In the example of the fifth aim, who is used as a picture for this idea?
questions.answer: A soldier standing before his king.

questions.question: What does the soldier wear in that example?
questions.answer: The honors and decorations given to him.

questions.question: What do those decorations help show?
questions.answer: The king’s favor to the soldier.

questions.question: In the fifth aim, whose view should a person remember?
questions.answer: Allah’s seeing and watching.

questions.question: What is the sixth aim about noticing in living things?
questions.answer: Their praising, worship, and turning to their Creator.

questions.question: After noticing these signs in living things, what should a person do?
questions.answer: Think about them, see their meaning, and bear witness to them.

questions.question: What are the small human qualities in the seventh aim used for?
questions.answer: They are used like little measures to understand Allah’s perfect qualities.

questions.question: Which three human qualities are named in the seventh aim?
questions.answer: Knowledge, power, and will.

questions.question: What example is given to explain this measuring idea?
questions.answer: A person arranges his house in an orderly way.

questions.question: If a person can organize a small house, what should that teach him about the Maker of the world?
questions.answer: That the Maker of the world has far greater power, knowledge, and wisdom.

questions.question: Are these gifts things like shoes and hats, or inner gifts and senses?
questions.answer: Inner gifts and senses.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a soldier meeting a king?
questions.answer: To help us understand showing thankful honor for gifts received.

questions.question: In the fifth aim, should a person act carelessly or with awareness?
questions.answer: With awareness.

questions.question: In the sixth aim, what do living beings show by being alive?
questions.answer: Signs that point to their Creator and praise Him.

questions.question: What three actions of living beings are mentioned in the sixth aim?
questions.answer: Greeting their Creator in their own way, glorifying Him, and worshiping Him.

questions.question: What should a person do after thinking about those actions?
questions.answer: Confirm them and make them known by testifying to them.

questions.question: In the seventh aim, why are human abilities called small samples?
questions.answer: Because they are tiny compared with Allah’s endless qualities.

questions.question: What can your own knowing teach you about Allah?
questions.answer: That Allah knows perfectly and completely.

questions.question: What can your own power teach you about Allah?
questions.answer: That Allah has perfect power.

questions.question: What is compared to a soldier’s medals in the fifth aim?
questions.answer: The beautiful inner abilities and senses given to a person.

questions.question: Who gave those inner abilities and senses?
questions.answer: Allah, through the showing of His names.

questions.question: What should a person remember when using those gifts?
questions.answer: To use them knowingly and thankfully.

questions.question: The sixth aim teaches a person to watch living things closely. What should the person notice?
questions.answer: That they show life, praise Allah, and serve Him.

questions.question: Does the sixth aim tell a person only to look, or also to think?
questions.answer: Also to think.

questions.question: After seeing those signs, what should a believer do with that truth?
questions.answer: Accept it and speak of it as true.

questions.question: In the seventh aim, what are people told to use as measuring tools?
questions.answer: Their own limited abilities.

questions.question: Which limited abilities are named?
questions.answer: Knowledge, power, and will.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention an orderly house?
questions.answer: To show that order points to a maker with skill and wisdom.

questions.question: If your house shows planning, what does the whole world show even more?
questions.answer: That its Maker is very powerful, knowing, and wise.

questions.question: Which aim is mostly about watching living beings worship?
questions.answer: The sixth aim.

questions.question: Which aim is mostly about learning about Allah from your own abilities?
questions.answer: The seventh aim.

questions.question: In the fifth aim, what should a person do with the beautiful qualities given to him?
questions.answer: Adorn himself with them in a conscious way.

questions.question: What picture is used to explain that idea simply?
questions.answer: A soldier wearing the honors from his ruler.

questions.question: What do the soldier’s honors show about his ruler?
questions.answer: That the ruler showed him favor.

questions.question: In the fifth aim, before whom does a person live and appear?
questions.answer: Before Allah, who sees all.

questions.question: In the sixth aim, what are the signs of life in living beings meant to show?
questions.answer: Their praise and worship of their Creator.

questions.question: What should happen after a person reflects on these signs?
questions.answer: He should recognize them and bear witness to them.

questions.question: In the seventh aim, are human qualities complete or limited?
questions.answer: Limited.

questions.question: Why are limited human qualities still useful?
questions.answer: They help us understand, in a small way, Allah’s perfect qualities.

questions.question: What does making a house neatly suggest about the person who made it?
questions.answer: That the person had knowledge, ability, and planning.

questions.question: What does the order of the world suggest about its Maker?
questions.answer: That He is perfectly powerful, knowing, and wise.

questions.question: What kind of “jewels” are mentioned in the fifth aim?
questions.answer: Fine inner senses and gifts, not real gemstones.

questions.question: In the fifth aim, what attitude should a person have toward these gifts?
questions.answer: Thankful awareness.

questions.question: In the sixth aim, what should a person learn from animals, plants, and other living things?
questions.answer: That their lives point to Allah and show praise and worship.

questions.question: What is one thing the sixth aim says living beings do toward their Creator?
questions.answer: They glorify Him.

questions.question: When a person reflects on these signs and tells the truth about them, what is he doing?
questions.answer: He is witnessing to what they show.

questions.question: In the seventh aim, what is the purpose of the small amount of power a person has?
questions.answer: To help him understand Allah’s much greater power.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the small amount of knowledge a person has?
questions.answer: To help him understand Allah’s perfect knowledge.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the small amount of will a person has?
questions.answer: To help him understand Allah’s perfect will.

questions.question: If a person sees great order in the world, what should he infer?
questions.answer: Its Maker has perfect wisdom and control.

questions.question: What does the fifth aim teach a person to do with Allah’s subtle gifts?
questions.answer: To wear them in a respectful way by using them knowingly.

questions.question: What story picture helps explain the fifth aim?
questions.answer: A soldier showing the honors he received from his king.

questions.question: What do those honors tell others?
questions.answer: That the king favored him.

questions.question: In the sixth aim, what should a person pay attention to in living beings?
questions.answer: Their life, praise, and worship.

questions.question: What should come after paying attention to those things?
questions.answer: Thinking deeply about them and confirming their meaning.

questions.question: What does “bearing witness” mean here in simple words?
questions.answer: Saying and showing that something is true.

questions.question: In the seventh aim, what are people supposed to use as little measuring sticks?
questions.answer: Their own small abilities.

questions.question: Name the three little measuring sticks mentioned.
questions.answer: Knowledge, power, and will.

questions.question: How does your own arranging of a home help you learn about the world?
questions.answer: It shows that order comes from someone who knows what he is doing.

questions.question: What does the much bigger order in the world teach about its Maker?
questions.answer: That He is far greater in power, knowledge, and wisdom.

questions.question: Which aim teaches learning by watching living beings?
questions.answer: The sixth aim.

questions.question: Which aim teaches learning by comparing your abilities with Allah’s perfect qualities?
questions.answer: The seventh aim.
